content: Creating an Action Create an action when a validated insight requires a coordinated response. title: Creating Your First Survey
excerpt: Creating Your First Survey Create a focused survey that connects a clear business objective to a relevant audience and actionable insight. The survey lifecycle 01 Plan 02 Design 03 Configure Audience 04 Publish 05 Collect Responses 06 Analy
content: Creating Your First Survey Create a focused survey that connects a clear business objective to a relevant audience and actionable insight. The survey lifecycle 01 Plan 02 Design 03 Configure Audience 04 Publish 05 Collect Responses 06 Analyse 07 Act 08 Improve Why this matters Effective surveys begin with decisions, not questions. A clear objective keeps the experience concise and makes it easier to act on the results. Before you begin Prepare a survey owner, objective, target audience, open and close dates, approved questions and a plan for reviewing results. Step by step 1. Open Survey Management and select Create survey . 2. Add a clear internal name, purpose and accountable owner. 3. Choose a Topic Template or start with approved repository questions. 4. Arrange sections and confirm response formats. 5. Configure the respondent audience and exclusions. 6. Set dates, invitation text and reminder rules. 7. Preview on desktop and mobile, then send an internal test. 8. Resolve validation issues and complete the publish review. Example A Customer Success team creates a 10 question onboarding survey for contacts who completed implementation in the previous 30 days. The survey maps results to Customer Engagement and includes one open text improvement prompt. Best practices Ask only questions that support a decision or action. Put essential questions early and group related topics. State the purpose and expected completion time. Avoid leading wording and unnecessary mandatory fields. Frequently asked questions Can a survey be changed after it is published? Changes may be restricted to protect response integrity. Review carefully before publication and create a new version when measurement content must change. Related articles Planning a Survey Publishing and Distributing a Survey Monitoring Survey Progress

title: Frequently Asked Questions
excerpt: Frequently Asked Questions Quick answers to common questions about configuring and using workSPOC Voice. What should I configure before creating my first survey? Set up the relevant organisation structure, users and permissions, VOC framewo
content: Frequently Asked Questions Quick answers to common questions about configuring and using workSPOC Voice. What should I configure before creating my first survey? Set up the relevant organisation structure, users and permissions, VOC framework, contacts, approved questions and survey governance. Can I reuse questions across surveys? Yes. Use approved questions from the Question Repository to improve consistency and comparison. What is the difference between a Pillar, Domain and Practice? A Pillar is a strategic area, a Domain is a measurable area within it, and a Practice is a specific capability or behaviour. Can I import customer contacts? Yes. Import prepared contact data, review validation messages and resolve duplicates before using it for an audience. Can different surveys use different customer groups? Yes. Respondent audiences can use classifications and other permitted contact attributes. Can a survey be changed after it is published? Measurement changes may be restricted to protect response integrity. Review and test carefully before publication. How do I monitor survey completion? Open the survey Progress view to review invited, delivered, opened, started and completed statuses. How do insights become improvement actions? Validate the evidence, create an action, assign an owner and define a due date and measurable outcome. Who can create or manage users? Only users with the appropriate administrative permission should add, change or disable users. Where can I find previously created questions? Search the Question Repository and check filters such as status, category and framework mapping. Related articles Quick Start Guide Troubleshooting Contact Support

title: From Insight to Action
excerpt: From Insight to Action Convert validated customer evidence into an owned improvement action with a measurable outcome. Why this matters A VOC programme creates value when the organisation responds. Action management makes the decision, owne
content: From Insight to Action Convert validated customer evidence into an owned improvement action with a measurable outcome. Why this matters A VOC programme creates value when the organisation responds. Action management makes the decision, ownership and outcome visible through the next measurement cycle. Before you begin Validate the insight, identify affected customers or processes, involve the team closest to the issue and agree what evidence will show improvement. How it works An action connects a finding to an owner, priority, due date, milestones and success measure. Progress can then be reviewed alongside the insight that prompted it. Step by step 1. Open the relevant insight and select Create action . 2. Write a specific outcome focused title. 3. Summarise the customer evidence and affected scope. 4. Assign one accountable owner and supporting contributors. 5. Set priority, due date and milestones. 6. Define a success measure and baseline. 7. Review progress regularly and attach evidence. 8. Close only after the outcome is verified. Example Insight: Strategic accounts report inconsistent implementation updates. Action: Introduce a weekly sponsor update for all strategic implementations within 30 days. Measure: Raise Proactive Communication from 61 to 72 in the next cycle. Best practices Address the cause, not simply the symptom. Keep one accountable owner per action. Use measures the owner can influence. Communicate completed improvements back to customers. Frequently asked questions How do insights become improvement actions? Create an action from validated evidence, assign ownership and define a measurable outcome. When should an action be closed? When agreed completion evidence and the success criteria have been reviewed—not merely when tasks are finished. Related articles Creating an Action Tracking Actions Measuring Improvement

title: Interpreting Results

content: Interpreting Results Interpret results by combining quantitative movement, respondent representation, qualitative context and business knowledge. A practical review 1. Validate data quality and sample context. 2. Identify material patterns, not isolated values. 3. Compare relevant segments and prior cycles. 4. Explore comments and themes. 5. title: Managing Contacts
excerpt: Managing Contacts Contacts form the audience for workSPOC Voice surveys and connect feedback to relevant customer entities. Why this matters Accurate, well classified contacts improve invitation delivery, audience selection and meaningful a
content: Managing Contacts Contacts form the audience for workSPOC Voice surveys and connect feedback to relevant customer entities. Why this matters Accurate, well classified contacts improve invitation delivery, audience selection and meaningful analysis while reducing duplicate or inappropriate outreach. How it works Customer entities represent organisations or accounts. Entity contacts connect people to an organisation and business relationship. Individual contacts represent respondents managed independently. Classification segments contacts as Customer, Distributor, Dealer, Partner, Supplier or Employee. Step by step 1. Open Control → Contacts . 2. Add or import customer entities first where account relationships matter. 3. Add contact names, email details, classification and relevant organisation attributes. 4. Link entity contacts to the correct customer entity. 5. Review import validation messages and resolve duplicates. 6. Create a filtered audience and verify sample records before survey use. Example A partner survey targets senior contacts at active distributor entities in APAC. Classification, region and role data create the audience without manually selecting every respondent. Best practices Import only permissioned, relevant contact data. Validate email addresses and required fields. Use stable identifiers to prevent duplicates. Refresh ownership and classification before each survey cycle. Frequently asked questions Can I import customer contacts? Yes. Prepare the file using the expected columns and review validation results before confirming. Can different surveys use different customer groups? Yes. Build audiences using contact attributes and classifications. Related articles Contact Classification Configuring Respondents Troubleshooting

title: Managing Users
excerpt: Managing Users Add colleagues to workSPOC Voice, provide appropriate access and keep permissions current. Why this matters Good access management protects customer information and ensures surveys, insights and actions are handled by account
content: Managing Users Add colleagues to workSPOC Voice, provide appropriate access and keep permissions current. Why this matters Good access management protects customer information and ensures surveys, insights and actions are handled by accountable people. Before you begin Confirm the person's business email, responsibilities, organisational scope and required role. Only authorised administrators should manage users. Step by step 1. Open Control → Manage Users and select Add user . 2. Enter the user's name and verified work email. 3. Select the role that most closely matches their responsibilities. 4. Limit organisational scope where appropriate. 5. Review permissions, then send the invitation. 6. Periodically review last activity and access. 7. Disable a user promptly when access is no longer required. Example A survey manager needs to build and monitor surveys but does not administer organisation settings. Assign the survey management role and relevant business unit scope instead of full administrative access. Best practices Apply least privilege access. Do not share user accounts. Review privileged users and leavers regularly. Disable rather than repurpose former user records. Frequently asked questions Who can create or manage users? Users with the appropriate administrative permission. What happens when a user is disabled? They can no longer access the platform; their historic work remains available for audit and continuity. Related articles User Roles & Access Manage Account Assigning Action Owners

title: Measuring Improvement
excerpt: Measuring Improvement Compare the agreed outcome measure with its baseline after enough time and evidence have accumulated. Use equivalent audiences and measures where possible, account for external changes and combine survey results with r
content: Measuring Improvement Compare the agreed outcome measure with its baseline after enough time and evidence have accumulated. Use equivalent audiences and measures where possible, account for external changes and combine survey results with relevant operational evidence. If the outcome did not improve, revisit the original insight and test a new hypothesis.

title: Monitoring Survey Progress
excerpt: Monitoring Survey Progress Track delivery, participation and completion while a survey is open. Why this matters Monitoring helps teams identify delivery problems early and use proportionate reminders without distorting the respondent exper
content: Monitoring Survey Progress Track delivery, participation and completion while a survey is open. Why this matters Monitoring helps teams identify delivery problems early and use proportionate reminders without distorting the respondent experience. How it works Survey status summarises invited, delivered, opened, started and completed responses. Filters can highlight patterns by audience segment or organisational dimension. Step by step 1. Open the live survey and select Progress . 2. Confirm invitations were delivered to the expected audience. 3. Review completion rate and compare it with the target. 4. Investigate bounced or invalid contact details. 5. Check whether specific segments are under represented. 6. Send a planned reminder to eligible non respondents. 7. Record any delivery decision and reassess before closing. Example After five days, overall completion is 38%, but partner participation is 18%. The owner checks delivery, confirms no technical issue and sends a targeted reminder with three days remaining. Best practices Agree response targets before launch. Focus on representation, not only the overall percentage. Limit reminders and honour opt outs. Do not interpret partial results as final conclusions. Frequently asked questions How do I monitor survey completion? Open the survey's Progress view to review invitation and response statuses. Why do invited and delivered totals differ? Invalid addresses, suppression rules or delivery failures can reduce the delivered count. Related articles Publishing and Distributing a Survey Closing a Survey Understanding Survey Responses

title: Publishing and Distributing a Survey
excerpt: Publishing and Distributing a Survey Complete final quality checks, publish the survey and deliver invitations to the intended audience. Why this matters Publication creates a live measurement event. Careful checks protect customer trust, d
content: Publishing and Distributing a Survey Complete final quality checks, publish the survey and deliver invitations to the intended audience. Why this matters Publication creates a live measurement event. Careful checks protect customer trust, delivery quality and the integrity of comparable responses. Before you begin Confirm approval, dates, audience size, sender details, invitation copy, privacy wording and an internal test response. Step by step 1. Open the survey's Review & publish area. 2. Resolve warnings for missing questions, respondents or required settings. 3. Preview the complete respondent experience. 4. Send a test invitation and complete it on desktop and mobile. 5. Confirm the final respondent count and remove exclusions. 6. Select Publish and verify the live status. 7. Start distribution using the configured invitation channel. 8. Review delivery status shortly after launch. Example A relationship survey is approved for 450 contacts. The owner tests links and translations, removes 12 opted out contacts and publishes at 09:00 in the audience's primary time zone. Best practices Use a recognisable sender and concise subject line. Avoid overlapping invitations to the same audience. Keep the survey window long enough for the audience context. Record the approved version and launch decision. Frequently asked questions Why can’t I publish? The survey may have no eligible respondents, no questions, invalid dates or another required setting missing. Can I add respondents later? Availability depends on survey status and governance. Validate the complete audience before publication where possible. Related articles Configuring Respondents Monitoring Survey Progress Troubleshooting

title: Question Repository
excerpt: Question Repository The Question Repository is the central, reusable library for survey questions. Why this matters Reusing validated wording improves respondent understanding, makes results comparable across surveys and reduces duplicated
content: Question Repository The Question Repository is the central, reusable library for survey questions. Why this matters Reusing validated wording improves respondent understanding, makes results comparable across surveys and reduces duplicated design work. How it works Questions can be searched and filtered by status, category, response format, framework mapping and topic. Approved questions can be reused in multiple surveys without rebuilding them. Step by step 1. Open Surveys → Question Repository . 2. Search before creating a new question. 3. Filter by category, topic or Pillar, Domain and Practice. 4. Review wording, response scale and usage notes. 5. Create or update content through the agreed approval process. 6. Select approved questions while designing a survey. Example An existing relationship question uses the organisation's standard five point scale. Reusing it in a regional survey preserves trend comparability and avoids introducing a subtly different measure. Best practices Give each question one clear purpose. Avoid combining two ideas in one question. Preserve approved wording when trend comparison matters. Retire duplicates without removing historic survey evidence. Frequently asked questions Can I reuse questions across surveys? Yes—that is a core purpose of the repository. Where can I find previously created questions? Search the Question Repository and adjust status or category filters if necessary. Related articles Topic Templates Question Categories Selecting Questions

title: Quick Start Guide
excerpt: Quick Start Guide Use this practical journey to prepare workSPOC Voice and complete your first Voice of Customer cycle. Before you begin Confirm your programme sponsor, primary administrator, target customer group and the business question
content: Quick Start Guide Use this practical journey to prepare workSPOC Voice and complete your first Voice of Customer cycle. Before you begin Confirm your programme sponsor, primary administrator, target customer group and the business question your first survey should answer. Your end to end journey 01 · FOUNDATION Configure Organisation 02 · PEOPLE Add Users 03 · MEASURE Configure VOC Framework 04 · AUDIENCE Add / Import Contacts 05 · CONTENT Prepare Question Library 06 · DESIGN Create Survey 07 · TARGET Select Respondents 08 · LAUNCH Publish Survey 09 · LISTEN Monitor Responses 10 · LEARN Review Insights 11 · ACT Create Actions 12 · IMPROVE Track Improvement Step by step 1. Configure the organisation. Add the operating year and the structural dimensions you intend to report against. 2. Add users. Give programme leads and contributors the minimum access needed for their responsibilities. 3. Configure the VOC framework. Agree Pillars, Domains and Practices before linking questions. 4. Prepare contacts. Import clean, permissioned contacts and classify them for audience selection. 5. Build the question library. Reuse approved wording and group common sets into Topic Templates. 6. Create and publish the survey. Check settings, audience, dates and invitation content before launch. 7. Monitor, analyse and act. Watch participation, interpret patterns and create actions with clear owners and due dates. Best practices Keep the first survey focused and short. Test with an internal contact before publishing. Define how results will be reviewed before invitations go out. Record a baseline so improvement can be measured later. Related articles First Time Setup Checklist Creating Your First Survey From Insight to Action

title: Setting Up Your Organisation
excerpt: Setting Up Your Organisation Organisation Setup creates the reporting structure used throughout workSPOC Voice. Why this matters A well designed structure lets teams analyse survey responses across meaningful dimensions and compare like wit
content: Setting Up Your Organisation Organisation Setup creates the reporting structure used throughout workSPOC Voice. Why this matters A well designed structure lets teams analyse survey responses across meaningful dimensions and compare like with like. It also prevents inconsistent labels from fragmenting reports. Before you begin Gather the current organisation hierarchy, reporting definitions, operating year and a named owner for future changes. How it works Configure only the dimensions relevant to your programme: Structural element Typical use Operating Year Align feedback cycles to the reporting period Division Separate major lines of business Business Unit Compare accountable operating teams Region Analyse geographical performance Location / Site Identify site level variation Department Route findings to internal owners Function Compare cross business capabilities Offering Understand products or services Step by step 1. Open Control → Organisation Setup . 2. Set the active Operating Year. 3. Add top level Divisions and Business Units. 4. Add Regions and Locations where geographic analysis is required. 5. Add Departments, Functions and Offerings used in reporting. 6. Review naming, parent relationships and active status. 7. Save the structure and test it with a sample contact or survey. Example Northstar Services configures two Divisions, three Regions and five Offerings. Its quarterly dashboard can then compare onboarding feedback across the APAC and EMEA regions while filtering to the Managed Support offering. Best practices Mirror reporting needs, not every detail in the HR system. Use names people recognise and avoid unexplained abbreviations. Nominate one structure owner and review inactive values quarterly. Avoid changing labels during a live measurement cycle. Frequently asked questions Do we need every structural element? No. Use only dimensions that support ownership, targeting or analysis. Can structure change later? Yes, but assess the effect on trends and historic reporting first. Related articles Business Catalog Managing Contacts Understanding Survey Insights

title: Topic Templates
excerpt: Topic Templates Topic Templates are reusable collections of questions that accelerate survey creation and standardise how a topic is measured. Why this matters Templates help distributed teams begin with governed content while still allowin
content: Topic Templates Topic Templates are reusable collections of questions that accelerate survey creation and standardise how a topic is measured. Why this matters Templates help distributed teams begin with governed content while still allowing a survey to reflect its audience and purpose. Before you begin Confirm that each included question is approved, current and uses compatible response scales where comparison is expected. Step by step 1. Open Surveys → Topic Templates . 2. Create a template with a specific name and purpose. 3. Search the Question Repository and add approved questions. 4. Arrange questions in a logical respondent journey. 5. Add guidance about when the template should be used. 6. Review and make the template available to survey designers. Example An Account Onboarding template contains eight approved questions covering clarity, timeliness, effort and early value. Regional teams reuse it and add at most two local questions. Best practices Keep templates focused and short. Assign an owner and review date. Use version notes when material wording changes. Treat templates as a strong starting point, not a reason to ask irrelevant questions. Related articles Question Repository Planning a Survey Creating Your First Survey

content: Tracking Actions Track milestones, risks and outcome measures throughout delivery. Update status at the agreed cadence, attach concise evidence and record material decisions. content: Trends & Comparisons Trends show how a consistent measure changes over time; comparisons show differences between relevant groups or periods. title: Troubleshooting
excerpt: Troubleshooting Use these checks to resolve common configuration and survey issues before contacting support. Common issues Problem Possible cause Suggested resolution Survey cannot be published No respondents or required configuration is m
content: Troubleshooting Use these checks to resolve common configuration and survey issues before contacting support. Common issues Problem Possible cause Suggested resolution Survey cannot be published No respondents or required configuration is missing Open the publish checklist, add eligible respondents and resolve every required item Contact not appearing in survey audience Incorrect classification or incomplete contact information Review the contact record, audience filters and required fields User cannot access a module Role or permission does not allow access Ask an administrator to compare the role with the user's responsibilities Question not appearing in survey Question filters or template selection may exclude it Clear filters, check approval status and confirm the template contains the question Survey invitation not received Incorrect contact information or email delivery issue Verify the address and delivery status; check suppression or bounce details Before escalating 1. Record the screen, survey or record affected. 2. Note the exact message and when it occurred. 3. Confirm whether other users or records are affected. 4. Check recent changes to permissions, filters or configuration. 5. Avoid repeatedly publishing or re importing while investigating. Frequently asked questions Will retrying create duplicates? Some actions can. Review current status before repeating an import, invitation or creation step. What should I include in a support request? Provide business impact, steps to reproduce, time, affected record and a screenshot without unnecessary personal data. Related articles Frequently Asked Questions Best Practices Contact Support

title: Understanding Pillars, Domains & Practices
excerpt: Understanding Pillars, Domains & Practices Pillars, Domains and Practices turn broad strategic priorities into consistent, measurable areas. Why this matters A shared hierarchy connects question design to analysis. Teams can see a high leve
content: Understanding Pillars, Domains & Practices Pillars, Domains and Practices turn broad strategic priorities into consistent, measurable areas. Why this matters A shared hierarchy connects question design to analysis. Teams can see a high level outcome, explore its contributing areas and identify a specific capability to improve. How it works Pillar — a high level strategic area the organisation wants to measure. Domain — a measurable area contained within a Pillar. Practice — a specific capability or behaviour within a Domain. Example hierarchy Pillar: Customer Experience → Domain: Customer Engagement → Practice: Proactive Communication Questions and survey insights can be linked back to these levels, supporting both executive summaries and detailed diagnosis. Step by step 1. Agree a small set of strategic Pillars. 2. Define distinct Domains under each Pillar. 3. Add observable, actionable Practices under each Domain. 4. Write plain language descriptions and assign ownership. 5. Map validated questions to the most relevant level. 6. Test whether results will lead to a clear conversation or action. Best practices Keep levels mutually clear and collectively useful. Define Practices as capabilities teams can influence. Avoid duplicate concepts under different labels. Govern framework changes between survey cycles. Frequently asked questions Can one question relate to more than one area? It may, but choose mappings carefully to avoid double counting or ambiguous analysis. How many levels are required? Use enough detail to diagnose performance without creating an unwieldy framework. Related articles Headers & Factors Question Repository Interpreting Results

title: Understanding Survey Insights
excerpt: Understanding Survey Insights Use survey insights to move from individual answers to defensible patterns, priorities and decisions. Why this matters Scores alone do not explain what to do. workSPOC Voice connects response evidence with the
content: Understanding Survey Insights Use survey insights to move from individual answers to defensible patterns, priorities and decisions. Why this matters Scores alone do not explain what to do. workSPOC Voice connects response evidence with the VOC framework and business dimensions so teams can find meaningful variation and identify improvement opportunities. Before you begin Confirm the survey is sufficiently complete, review the respondent mix and understand the scale, benchmark and filter context. How it works Insights can be explored by survey, question, Pillar, Domain, Practice and relevant organisational or contact dimensions. Quantitative trends and response themes should be considered together. Step by step 1. Open Insights → Survey Insights and select a survey cycle. 2. Check response volume and audience representation. 3. Review headline results and movement from the comparison period. 4. Explore Pillars, then drill into contributing Domains and Practices. 5. Apply one filter at a time and note the comparison baseline. 6. Read qualitative comments and response themes for context. 7. Record evidence, confidence and an accountable next step. Example Overall Customer Experience is stable, but Proactive Communication declines by nine points among strategic accounts in one region. Comments consistently mention delayed status updates, providing a specific improvement hypothesis. Best practices Check sample size before comparing small segments. Distinguish correlation from proven cause. Look for consistent evidence across scores, trends and comments. Protect respondent confidentiality when sharing results. Frequently asked questions Why does a dashboard result change when I apply a filter? The calculation now reflects only responses that match the selected criteria. Does the lowest score always become the top priority? No. Consider strategic importance, trend, reach, confidence and ability to act. Related articles Trends & Comparisons Interpreting Results From Insight to Action

content: Understanding Survey Responses A response is a respondent's submitted evidence for a survey. Interpret it in the context of the question, response scale, survey timing and audience. Check completion status, sample size and missing data before aggregating. Protect confidentiality and avoid drawing conclusions from identifiable comments or very small groups. content: User Roles & Access Roles group permissions for common responsibilities. Access may also be limited by organisational scope. Best practices Give users only the access required for their work. Separate administration from ordinary survey tasks where practical. Review privileged access and inactive users regularly. Update access when responsibilities change. See Managing Users for the user lifecycle.

content: Welcome to workSPOC workSPOC Voice is an enterprise Voice of Customer platform that helps teams turn customer feedback into coordinated, measurable improvements. Why this matters Customer evidence is most useful when it is connected to the business, analysed consistently and owned through to action. workSPOC brings configuration, surveys, insight and improvement into one operating rhythm. How it works Teams configure their organisation and measurement framework, prepare customers and questions, run surveys, interpret results and create owned actions. Each stage builds on the one before it. :::tip A good first visit Start with the Quick Start Guide, then use the checklist to confirm your setup. ::: What you can do Model the organisation and customer landscape. Maintain a reusable VOC framework and question library. Design and distribute targeted surveys. Compare responses and identify themes. Assign actions and track measurable improvement. Example A regional service team surveys key accounts after delivery. Results are segmented by region and offering, revealing that proactive communication is weakest in one business unit. The team assigns an action owner, improves the contact cadence and measures the next survey cycle. Best practices Agree measurement outcomes before configuring the platform. Use clear naming conventions across organisational structures. Keep permissions and contacts current. Close the loop by communicating actions to stakeholders. Related articles What is workSPOC Voice?
